title: Describing a town
goal: Name places in town, use location words, and describe the town where you live.
bekal: using location words that end in *de*
describing your town in five sentences

dialogs.title: Diálogo — En la oficina de turismo
dialogs.intro: Now it's time to describe a whole town, not just one building.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Buenos días. ¿Qué hay que ver en la ciudad?
lines.id: Good morning. What is there to see in this town?
lines.literal: good day. what there-is that see in the town?

lines.speaker: Empleada:
lines.text: Mucho. La catedral es preciosa y está en el centro.
lines.id: Lots. The cathedral is very beautiful, and it's in the center.
lines.literal: much. the cathedral is pretty and it-is-located in the center.

lines.text: Hay tres. El más interesante está detrás de la plaza.
lines.id: There are three. The most interesting one is behind the square.

notes: **¿Qué hay que ver?** = "what is there to see?" The pattern *hay que + verb* means "one needs to / one must" without saying who: *hay que pagar aquí* (you pay here). Compare *tengo que pagar* (I have to pay) from Unit 7 — one is general, the other personal.
**El más interesante** = "the most interesting (one)". The superlative is simply *el / la / los / las + más + adjective*: *la ciudad más bonita*, *los museos más antiguos*.
**Poder (can)** also changes inside, like *querer*: *puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, podéis, pueden*. It's always followed by the dictionary form: *puedo comer*, *¿puedes ayudarme?*
**De … a …** works for any range — time, days, hours: *de martes a domingo*, *de diez a ocho*, *de Madrid a Barcelona*.
**Algo típico.** An adjective after *algo* and *nada* is always masculine singular: *algo típico*, *nada especial*, *algo barato*.
**Muchos restaurantes buenos** — notice both go plural: the quantity word *muchos* and the adjective *buenos*. Adjectives agree with their noun, not with the word next to them.
**Gratis** never changes form: *es gratis*, *son gratis*, *entrada gratis*. One of the few immune adjectives.
**Bus numbers are said as plain numbers**, and you'll be understood even without *número*: *el doce va directo*.

grammars.title: Location words
body: Almost all of them end in *de*, and *de + el* must merge into *del*: *al lado del banco*, *cerca del centro*, *enfrente del museo*.
after: *Enfrente de* and *delante de* often get mixed up. *Delante de* means right in front of something (you stand in front of the door); *enfrente de* means across from it, usually with a street in between.
When the reference point is clear from context, drop the *de* and let the location word stand alone: *El banco está enfrente.* — the bank is over the road.

blocks.text: The speaking practice that pays off fastest at A1: describe the town where you live in five sentences. Here's the frame.

blocks.title: A five-sentence frame
items: **Vivo en …** — name the city and country. *Vivo en Bandung, en Indonesia.*
**Es una ciudad …** — what it's like, with *ser*: *grande*, *pequeña*, *tranquila*, *ruidosa*, *bonita*, *moderna*, *antigua*.
**Está en …** — where it is, with *estar*: *en el norte / sur / este / oeste de Java*, *cerca de Yakarta*, *en las montañas*.
**En mi ciudad hay …** — what's there: *muchas tiendas*, *dos universidades*, *un mercado muy grande*.
**Lo que más me gusta es …** — the part you like best. *Lo que más me gusta es el clima.*

blocks.title: Towns built around a square
items: Almost every town in Spain and Latin America has a *plaza mayor* — a square with a church on one side and the town hall on another. If you get lost, head there: from the square, every street is easy to read.
*El paseo* is the habit of strolling in the early evening, usually before dinner, just to get out and see the neighbors. It isn't exercise, and there's no particular destination.
Addresses put the number **after** the street name: *Calle Mayor 25*, not *25 Calle Mayor*. The floor comes separately: *Calle Mayor 25, 3.º B* — third floor, door B.
And watch the floors: *la planta baja* is the ground floor, so *el primer piso* is what Americans call the second floor.

exercises.prompt: Fill in the right location word to match the meaning.
items: El banco está ____ de la farmacia. (next to)
El museo está ____ de la plaza. (behind)
El libro está ____ de la mesa. (on top of)
La tienda está ____ el banco y el café. (between)
Mi casa está ____ del centro. (far from)

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to make a correct Spanish sentence.
items: banco / ¿ / hay / aquí / un / por / ?
farmacia / la / al / de / lado / está
cerrado / lunes / los / está
ciudad / mi / grande / es
¿ / está / dónde / estación / la / ?

answers: al lado — detrás — encima — entre — lejos
What is there to see in the town? — The most interesting one is behind the square. — How many minutes away is the beach? — You pay at the entrance. — Straight ahead and then left.
¿Hay un banco por aquí? — Está al lado de la farmacia. — Los lunes está cerrado. — Mi ciudad es grande. — ¿Dónde está la estación?
